channel.title: Llm-Ops on Junho Lee
channel.description: Recent content in Llm-Ops on Junho Lee

item.title: Taming Multi-Agent Context Overload with a Git Priority Queue
item.description: A solo experiment replacing 20 scattered AI coding terminal threads with Git-committed Markdown tickets, an owner inbox, and single-ticket context closure.

item.title: Controlling LLM Operating Costs for Enterprise AI Agents
item.description: How enterprises measure repeated base inputs, accumulated context, and call counts separately while cutting exploration loops with ontology search and a Solution Cache.

item.title: How Uber Controls AI Coding Costs Across Models, Cache, and Tools
item.description: Uber kept total AI agent spend stable despite a 9.4x jump in weekly requests by breaking down cost drivers and tuning model routing, cache TTLs, and MCP tool loading.

item.title: Persistent Subagent Memory Scopes and Design in Claude Code
item.description: Claude Code adds persistent memory across User, Project, and Local scopes so custom subagents retain context across sessions without cluttering the main thread.

item.title: Tuning Codex Settings to Preserve GPT-5.6 Quality and API Quota
item.description: Fix truncated reasoning and runaway API quota drain on GPT-5.6 in Codex by replacing the 30-second reporting prompt and capping subagent spawning in config.toml.

item.title: 12. Racing Three Coding Agents in Isolated Git Worktrees
item.description: Running multiple coding agents in one checkout kept breaking my builds. I moved to git worktree isolation and a race workflow: three different models on the same task, with the open-source tool Orca handling the setup.

item.title: Cutting Claude Fable 5 Token Usage by 90% Through Role Delegation
item.description: A practical orchestration guide to reducing Claude Fable 5 token costs by up to 90% by tuning thinking effort and delegating work across Opus 4.8 and Haiku.

item.title: Oh My Hermes: A Workflow Skill Pack Extending Hermes Agent
item.description: Oh My Hermes (OMH) adds structured multi-step workflows, subagent orchestration, and explicit handoff gates to Hermes Agent as an open-source skill pack.

item.title: Loop Engineering Tools for Preventing Runaway AI Coding Agents
item.description: Design explicit goals, validation commands, budgets, stop rules, and human approval gates so AI coding agents run safely without infinite loops or cost spikes.

item.title: ECC: An Open-Source Operator System for Optimizing AI Agent Performance
item.description: Explore ECC, an open-source operator system that optimizes token usage, preserves session memory, and enables continuous skill extraction for Claude Code and Cursor.

item.title: Three Core Skills and Portfolio Strategies for Aspiring AI PMs
item.description: Moving from deterministic software to probabilistic AI products requires AI literacy, distribution-aware metrics, failure design, and documented build logs.

item.title: 12 Engineering Tricks to Turn Codex into an Autonomous Dev System
item.description: Practical workflow patterns that pair Codex, ChatGPT, MCP servers, remote handoffs, and subagents into a multi-model engineering control plane.

item.title: Operating an AI-Native Startup with Agents and Overnight Learning Loops
item.description: How AI-native startups delegate routine execution to agents, run overnight feedback loops, and shift engineers toward system architecture and reliability.

item.title: Building a Cross-Verification Workflow with Claude Code and Codex
item.description: Separating author and reviewer roles across Claude Code and Codex catches blind spots before merge without blocking developer workflows.

item.title: Hermes WebUI: Multi-Profile Context Isolation and Browser Control for Agents
item.description: Hermes WebUI brings the Hermes autonomous agent into the browser with isolated specialist profiles, visual tool-call cards, and built-in file editing.

item.title: 10. Spider 72%: The Dataset, Not the Model, Shapes the Error Profile
item.description: Switching to Pro actually dropped accuracy by 8%p. I categorized 19 errors into 6 types and ran the same pipeline on Spider. The distributions were completely different. DB characteristics determine the error profile more than the model does.

item.title: 9. BIRD 56%: Nine Experiments and What Got Ruled Out
item.description: I hit 80% on my own 30-question benchmark, but only 56% on BIRD Mini-Dev’s 50 public questions. Nine experiments later, I had ruled out the multi-candidate hypothesis from three different angles. What’s left is schema understanding and methodology.

item.title: Practical Agent Design Lessons from the OpenAI Guide
item.description: Handing open-ended planning to an LLM causes production loops and stalls. OpenAI’s practical guide solves this with explicit state-machine workflow control.

item.title: Directory Structure and Written SOPs for Multi-Agent Workflows
item.description: Deploying AI agents without workspace structure scatters outputs. Mirroring an org chart in directories and writing explicit SOPs stabilizes quality.

item.title: Cutting Claude Code Setup Friction with Plugin Advisor
item.description: Plugin Advisor narrows down Claude Code configuration using project-specific Preset Packs and pre-flight checklists that catch missing keys before runtime.

item.title: Hands-On Jupyter Notebooks for LangChain v1, LangGraph, and Deep Agents
item.description: Legacy chain examples broke with LangChain v1. This Jupyter notebook repository walks step by step through State and Node control in LangGraph and Deep Agents.
